sentences.text: Look at a pencil.
It is a thin piece of wood.
Inside it there is a grey stick.
Most people call this lead.
sentences.translationRu: Многие называют это грифелем из свинца.

sentences.text: But there is no lead in a pencil.
There never was.
The grey part is graphite.
Graphite is a kind of carbon.
It comes out of the ground.
It is soft and it is black.
Diamonds are carbon too.
The same thing, in a different shape.
sentences.translationRu: То же вещество, только другой формы.

sentences.text: One is the hardest thing we know.
sentences.translationRu: Одно — самое твёрдое, что мы знаем.

sentences.text: The other one draws a line.
Graphite is made of flat sheets.
The sheets slide over each other.
When you write, some sheets come off.
sentences.translationRu: Когда ты пишешь, часть слоёв остаётся на бумаге.

sentences.text: They stay on the paper.
That is your line.
So a pencil does not put ink on paper.
sentences.translationRu: То есть карандаш не наносит чернила.

sentences.text: It leaves small pieces of itself.
The graphite is not pure.
It is mixed with clay.
More clay makes a harder pencil.
A hard pencil draws a light line.
Less clay makes a soft pencil.
A soft pencil draws a dark line.
That is what the letters mean.
sentences.translationRu: Вот что означают буквы на карандаше.

sentences.text: H is for hard.
B is for black.
HB is in the middle.
Now think about the wood.
The wood is not there to look nice.
Graphite breaks very easily.
Hold a thin stick of it and press.
It will break in your hand.
The wood holds it together.
It also keeps your fingers clean.
One pencil can draw a long line.
sentences.translationRu: Одним карандашом можно провести длинную линию.

sentences.text: People say about fifty kilometres.
Nobody has really tried it.
But it can write under water.
It can write in very cold places.
It can write in space.
A pen cannot do any of that.
So the pencil is still here.
sentences.translationRu: Поэтому карандаш всё ещё с нами.

sentences.text: It has not changed in two hundred years.
sentences.translationRu: За двести лет он почти не изменился.

sentences.text: Almost every old city has a square.
sentences.translationRu: Почти в каждом старом городе есть площадь.

sentences.text: An open space with nothing built on it.
sentences.translationRu: Открытое место, где ничего не построено.

sentences.text: In the middle of expensive land.
That is strange when you think about it.
Land in a city centre costs a fortune.
sentences.translationRu: Земля в центре города стоит целое состояние.

sentences.text: Leaving it empty looks like waste.
But squares are older than city planning.
They were not designed.
They were left over.
A market needs somewhere to stand.
Carts need somewhere to turn around.
Animals need somewhere to be counted.
So the space stayed open by use.
sentences.translationRu: Так место и осталось открытым — от пользования.

sentences.text: Then buildings grew around the edges.
The church took one side.
The town hall took another.
Merchants built along the rest.
Everything important faced the same hole.
sentences.translationRu: Всё важное смотрело в одну и ту же пустоту.

sentences.text: That is not an accident either.
A square is where a city can see itself.
sentences.translationRu: Площадь — это место, где город видит сам себя.

sentences.text: Announcements were made there.
Punishments happened there.
Markets, festivals, executions, elections.
All of it in the same rectangle.
The word forum means exactly this.
A place where a crowd becomes a public.
Which is why squares are political.
A crowd in a street is a queue.
A crowd in a square is a statement.
Governments have always known this.
Some cities widened their squares.
Others narrowed them on purpose.
Some planted trees in the middle.
Trees look generous.
They also break up a crowd.
Modern cities build fewer squares.
Land is priced by the square metre now.
sentences.translationRu: Землю теперь считают по квадратным метрам.

sentences.text: An empty metre earns nothing.
So new districts get roads and blocks.
sentences.translationRu: Поэтому в новых районах дороги и кварталы.

sentences.text: And people meet in shopping centres.
sentences.translationRu: А люди встречаются в торговых центрах.

sentences.text: Which are private, and have opening hours.
And where standing still is discouraged.
sentences.translationRu: И где стоять просто так не приветствуется.

sentences.text: That is the quiet difference.
sentences.translationRu: В этом и вся тихая разница.

sentences.text: A square belongs to nobody.
A shopping centre belongs to someone.
You can sit in a square for an hour.
Nobody will ask why.

title: Why bread tastes different in every country

sentences.text: Bread is four things.
Flour, water, salt, and something to raise it.
sentences.translationRu: Мука, вода, соль и то, что его поднимает.

sentences.text: That is the entire list.
And yet bread in one country
sentences.translationRu: И при этом хлеб в одной стране

sentences.text: is not remotely the bread in another.
sentences.translationRu: совершенно не похож на хлеб в другой.

sentences.text: The differences come from the margins.
Start with the flour.
Wheat varies enormously by climate.
sentences.translationRu: Пшеница сильно меняется в зависимости от климата.

sentences.text: Hot dry summers produce hard wheat.
sentences.translationRu: Жаркое сухое лето даёт твёрдую пшеницу.

sentences.text: Hard wheat carries more protein.
More protein means more gluten.
Gluten is what holds gas in the dough.
So that flour rises tall and chewy.
sentences.translationRu: Поэтому такая мука даёт высокий упругий хлеб.

sentences.text: Cool wet climates produce soft wheat.
sentences.translationRu: Прохладный влажный климат даёт мягкую пшеницу.

sentences.text: Less protein, less structure.
That flour makes a flatter, tenderer loaf.
sentences.translationRu: Такая мука даёт более плоский и нежный хлеб.

sentences.text: Neither is better.
Each country learned to bake what grew there.
sentences.translationRu: Каждая страна научилась печь из того, что росло.

sentences.text: Then the water, which nobody thinks about.
sentences.translationRu: Дальше вода, о которой никто не думает.

sentences.text: Hard water is full of minerals.
Minerals tighten gluten.
Soft water leaves the dough slack.
Bakers who move cities complain about this.
sentences.translationRu: Пекари, переезжающие в другой город, на это жалуются.

sentences.text: The same recipe stops working.
Then time, which matters most.
sentences.translationRu: И наконец время — оно важнее всего.

sentences.text: Yeast makes gas, and gas makes holes.
sentences.translationRu: Дрожжи дают газ, газ даёт дырки.

sentences.text: But yeast also makes acids.
Acids are where flavour lives.
Gas arrives in an hour.
Flavour takes considerably longer.
Industrial bread is finished in two hours.
sentences.translationRu: Промышленный хлеб готов за два часа.

sentences.text: It has risen and it has almost no taste.
sentences.translationRu: Он поднялся — и почти не имеет вкуса.

sentences.text: Which is why it is sold sliced and soft.
sentences.translationRu: Поэтому его продают нарезанным и мягким.

sentences.text: Those are the only qualities it has.
Sourdough takes a day, sometimes three.
sentences.translationRu: Хлеб на закваске делают день, иногда три.

sentences.text: It uses wild yeast from the air.
sentences.translationRu: Он берёт дикие дрожжи из воздуха.

sentences.text: And bacteria that live alongside it.
Those bacteria differ from place to place.
sentences.translationRu: Эти бактерии в разных местах разные.

sentences.text: So a starter carries a location in it.
sentences.translationRu: Поэтому закваска несёт в себе место.

sentences.text: Bakers talk about this almost mystically.
sentences.translationRu: Пекари говорят об этом почти мистически.

sentences.text: The science is duller and more interesting.
It is a small ecosystem you keep alive.
sentences.translationRu: Это маленькая экосистема, которую ты поддерживаешь живой.

sentences.text: And feed, and occasionally kill.
So four ingredients become a hundred breads.
sentences.translationRu: Так четыре ингредиента дают сотню хлебов.

sentences.text: None of the variation is in the list.
sentences.translationRu: И ни одно различие не записано в списке.

sentences.text: All of it is in the conditions.

title: The work that disappears when it is done well

sentences.text: Some jobs are visible only when they fail.
sentences.translationRu: Некоторые работы заметны, только когда они провалены.

sentences.text: Nobody notices clean water.
Everybody notices dirty water.
Nobody notices a bridge that holds.
sentences.translationRu: Никто не замечает мост, который стоит.

sentences.text: The whole country notices one that does not.
sentences.translationRu: Тот, который не стоит, замечает вся страна.

sentences.text: This is the structural problem of maintenance.
Its success is indistinguishable from nothing.
The consequences run deeper than gratitude.
Budgets are argued for in public.
A new hospital can be opened.
Somebody can cut a ribbon in front of it.
Repairing the roof of an old one cannot.
So the new building gets funded.
And the old roof waits.
It waits until it becomes an emergency.
At which point it costs several times more.
sentences.translationRu: И тогда обходится в несколько раз дороже.

sentences.text: This pattern repeats across every institution.
sentences.translationRu: Эта схема повторяется в любом учреждении.

sentences.text: Software has its own version of it.
sentences.translationRu: У софта своя версия того же.

sentences.text: A new feature is demonstrable.
Fixing the thing underneath it is not.
sentences.translationRu: Починку того, что под ней, показать нельзя.

sentences.text: So the underneath accumulates damage.
Until a small change costs three weeks.
sentences.translationRu: Пока мелкая правка не начинает стоить трёх недель.

sentences.text: Engineers have a phrase for the debt.
sentences.translationRu: У инженеров для этого долга есть название.

sentences.text: Managers rarely have a budget line for it.
sentences.translationRu: У руководителей для него редко есть статья расходов.

sentences.text: The people who do this work know the trap.
sentences.translationRu: Люди, которые этим занимаются, ловушку знают.

sentences.text: Do the job perfectly and you look unnecessary.
sentences.translationRu: Сделай работу идеально — и покажешься лишним.

sentences.text: Do it badly and you look incompetent.
There is no version where you look good.
sentences.translationRu: Варианта, в котором ты выглядишь хорошо, нет.

sentences.text: The incentive is quietly perverse.
A visible rescue is rewarded.
A crisis that never happened is not.
So systems drift towards heroism.
sentences.translationRu: И системы дрейфуют в сторону героизма.

sentences.text: And away from the boring work that prevents it.
sentences.translationRu: И прочь от скучной работы, которая его предотвращает.

sentences.text: Some organisations have tried to fix this.
The methods are unglamorous and they work.
Book maintenance as ordinary scheduled time.
sentences.translationRu: Заносить обслуживание в расписание как обычную работу.

sentences.text: Not as something done when there is slack.
sentences.translationRu: А не как то, что делают, когда есть окно.

sentences.text: Measure what did not break.
Which is harder than counting repairs.
And treat a quiet year as a result.
Rather than as an absence of results.
None of that is a management insight.
sentences.translationRu: Ничего из этого не управленческое откровение.

sentences.text: It is just refusing an obvious illusion.
sentences.translationRu: Это просто отказ от очевидной иллюзии.

sentences.text: The illusion that nothing happening
means that nothing is being done.
sentences.translationRu: означает, что ничего и не делается.
